keys.title: SSH keys (bastion)
keys.desc: Public keys allowed to open the Obliance SSH bastion. Only key authentication is accepted — never passwords.
keys.name: Name
keys.publicKeyHint: Content of your .pub file (ed25519, ECDSA or RSA ≥ 2048). Never paste the private key.
keys.addFailed: Failed to add the SSH key
keys.confirmDelete: Delete the SSH key "{{name}}"? It will no longer open the bastion.
keys.need2fa: Two-factor authentication must be enabled on your account to register an SSH key.

connect.title: Connect
connect.help: Once connected, type "help": "list" shows the machines you can reach, "ssh <machine>" opens a shell on it.
connect.hostKey: Server fingerprint (check it on first connection)
connect.enforceHint: Access is limited to authorized IPs: use the "SSH" button in the header to authorize your current IP.
connect.notRunning: The bastion is enabled but not running — contact an administrator.
connect.proxyJumpTitle: Native ProxyJump (Linux machines — scp, sftp, VS Code Remote…)
connect.proxyJumpHelp: The target account is always "obli" (then "sudo -i" for root). A one-time entry for your key is installed on the machine only while you connect. Requires an up-to-date agent.

button.title: SSH bastion
button.authorizeHint: A two-factor code is requested. Only this IP is authorized, and only for the SSH bastion.
button.authorized: This IP can connect over SSH for {{duration}}
button.authorizedFor: SSH authorized for this IP ({{time}} left)
button.revoked: SSH authorization revoked for this IP
button.need2fa: Enable two-factor authentication on your account to authorize an IP.
button.notEnforced: IP restriction is currently disabled by an administrator: any IP can connect with a valid key.
button.relayed: Obliance cannot see your real IP (internal relay address): SSH access is impossible from here. Contact an administrator.
button.allowlisted: This IP is in the administrator allow-list: SSH access is open without the button.
button.grantDisabled: IP authorization is disabled on this tenant ("Trust this IP" duration = 0). Ask an administrator to add your IP to the allow-list.
button.copyFailed: Could not copy — select the command and copy it manually

admin.title: SSH bastion
admin.enabledNotRunning: Enabled but not running — check the server logs
admin.howToEnable: To enable it, set SSH_BASTION_ENABLED=true (and optionally SSH_BASTION_PORT) in .env, publish the port in docker-compose.yml, then restart the server.
admin.enforceDesc: Only IPs from the allow-list below, or authorized by a user through the "SSH" button (2FA, for the 2FA "Trust this IP" duration), can open a session. An IP refused 3 times is banned.
admin.confirmDisableEnforce: Disable IP enforcement? Any IP holding a valid key will be able to reach the bastion, and refused IPs will no longer be banned.
admin.allowlistEmpty: The allow-list is empty: only IPs authorized through the "SSH" button can connect.

sshConfig.title: SSH profile for this Obliance
sshConfig.hintConfig: Add to ~/.ssh/config (Windows: %USERPROFILE%\.ssh\config). Then: "ssh {{alias}}" for the bastion, "ssh <machine>.{{alias}}" to jump to a machine (scp, sftp, VS Code Remote too).
sshConfig.hintScript: Appends the profile to your SSH config. Then: "ssh {{alias}}" for the bastion, "ssh <machine>.{{alias}}" to jump to a machine.

thresholds.title: Metric thresholds
thresholds.helpDevice: Leave empty to inherit from the group (then the system default).
thresholds.helpGroup: Leave empty to inherit the system default.

perDisk.empty: No internal disks reported by the agent yet.
perDisk.helper: Override the global disk threshold for a specific mount point — useful for system partitions that are full by nature, or for data drives that need tighter alerts. Removable / ISO mounts are always excluded.
perDisk.title: Per-disk override
perDisk.diskAlertsOff: Disk alerts are off: every disk is muted. Turn the Disk alerts switch back on to choose disk by disk.

thresholds.globalHelp: Default applied to ALL tenants. Each tenant can override it under /policies → Thresholds. Leave a field empty to use the system default (grey placeholder).
thresholds.tenantHelp: Every group and device of this tenant inherits these values unless set at its own level. Leave a field empty to inherit from the global layer (grey placeholder).
thresholds.alertsOffHint: Off: the status colour is still shown, but no notification (web, channels, mobile app) is sent for this metric.

customSections.autoRefreshHint: Re-run the script at a fixed cadence so the panel acts as a live dashboard.
customSections.commandHint: Initially intended for a single command (htop, top, etc.) but accepts a full script too. PowerShell scripts can output an HTML document — see render mode below. The Dashboard builder generates a self-contained script from a sample output if you want a kickstart.

customSections.empty: No custom sections yet. Click "New section" to create one.
customSections.htmlPtyNote: PTY is forced off for HTML output — terminal control sequences corrupt the document. Sandboxed iframe means scripts/forms are blocked, only static HTML + CSS render.
customSections.intervalHint: The cycle starts when the previous run exits — a 30s interval on a 5s script means a refresh every ~35s. Minimum 1s, max 3600s (1h).
customSections.intro: Custom sections appear as dedicated tabs between Remote and Explorer on each targeted device. Clicking the tab opens a read-only console that streams the configured command's live output. The process is killed when the tab is closed.
customSections.renderHtmlHint: Script writes a full HTML page (e.g. PowerShell ConvertTo-Html) — rendered in a sandboxed panel.
customSections.renderTerminalHint: Live xterm console — htop, tail -f, anything CLI.
customSections.title: Custom Sections
customSections.usePtyHint: Required for curses apps: htop, top, less, watch...
